evidence_quotes: 38 seismic events were recorded globally between 2026-02-09 and 2026-02-15, ranging from magnitude 4.0 to 5.7 and averaging magnitude 4.56
Tobelo, Indonesia led all regions with 5 events, followed by Nikolski, Alaska with 4 events
a magnitude 5.7 at 152.9 km depth on 2026-02-14 — the largest event in the dataset
a shallow magnitude 4.5 at only 3.3 km depth on the same date
rising from 2 events on 2026-02-11 to a peak of 9 events on 2026-02-14, before partially subsiding to 6 on 2026-02-15
a magnitude 4.9 at shallow depth (8.5 km) and a magnitude 4.1 at near-surface depth (1.9 km)
Tsunami warning status is recorded as false for all sampled events
criticisms: Minor: The report states the Nikolski magnitude 5.1 event is at '14.2 km depth' — this is correctly traceable to the digest (2026-02-14T08:32:21, depth_km: 14.2). No error here.

Minor: The report describes the Nikolski sequence as 'sustained shallow seismicity' but one Nikolski event is at 146.2 km depth (2026-02-14T05:03:42) — characterizing the full sequence as 'shallow' is a slight overstatement, though not a fabrication since two of the four events are indeed shallow.

Minor: The report says Mohr, Iran events were 'clustered within approximately 24 hours (2026-02-12 to 2026-02-13)' — the digest shows three Mohr events: 2026-02-12T18:22, 2026-02-12T21:59, and 2026-02-13T13:17, which spans roughly 19 hours, so '24 hours' is a slight rounding but not a fabrication.
